title: Thoryn provisioning fix request (thoryn-provision-request.json)
description: SSO-3710 (epic SSO-3304; oauthy ADR 2026-10-15-missing-rights-fix-path-cli-and-web-consent §1) — the ONE file a red provisioning job writes (`thoryn login --connection --fix-request <file>` on an invalid_client refusal whose only local mismatch is the GitHub environment; `thoryn provision plan|apply --fix-request <file>` on a plan with access_* rows) and uploads as the run artifact `thoryn-provision-request`. It names every RIGHT the repository's identity is missing and the exact CLI command a WORKSPACE ADMIN runs to grant it. It is a HYPOTHESIS, never a credential: a consumer (the Thoryn GitHub App, SSO-3711/3712) takes repository ids, run id and head sha from GitHub's own workflow_run record and DISCARDS the copies carried here; it re-reads the declared .thoryn/ file at the run's head sha and matches the trust on its pins, never on `trust.name`. Nothing in this file grants anything. It carries no secret: ids, names, commands. The `cli` string of each item is the SAME text the CLI prints on stderr — one rendering, in the CLI.

cliVersion.description: The `thoryn` CLI that wrote the file (`thoryn --version`), or null when unknown.

repository.description: The repository the job ran for — from the job's OIDC claims (`repository`, `repository_id`, `repository_owner_id`) at sign-in, from the runner's `GITHUB_REPOSITORY*` variables at plan time. A HINT: the consumer binds to GitHub's record of the run, not to these.

run.description: The run (`GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_SHA`) and the GitHub environment the job declared (the OIDC token's `environment` claim). A HINT, rebound by the consumer.

workspace.description: The workspace slug the identity signs in to (connection.json `workspace.slug`; the session's workspace at plan time).

file.description: `provision plan|apply` only: the provisioning file that was planned, as given, and its `sha256:` digest — so the consumer re-reads it at the run's head sha and drops any item naming an object the file does not declare. Null for a sign-in refusal.

trust.description: The workload identity trust the identity presents. `clientId` is the trust's `wi_…` workload client (known from the connection or the session); `plane` the environment the trust lives in (`production` for the plane without one); `applyEnvironment` the GitHub environment the trust pins for apply when known; `name` and `id` only when the producer could resolve them (a refused sign-in holds no token, so both are null there; a plan session resolves them when it may list trusts). The consumer matches the trust on PINS against GitHub's record of the run — the name is a hint to disambiguate, never the key.

missing.description: The rights that are missing, one item per refused row (or the one plan_profile item of a refused sign-in); SSO-3774 — one item per RIGHT: rows that need the same kind on the same object for the same subject (a declared trust the identity cannot see, and every application naming it) are one item, with the first row's reason. Empty when every failed row is a file fix (see `notes`).

notes.description: Failed rows that are NOT a missing right — the FILE must change (a differing read-only reference, a trust the file cannot declare, a scope the identity does not hold, a create whose parent is the workspace, a connection.json that names no apply environment) — so the request says so instead of staying silent.

options.description: SSO-3723 — the TWO options the log printed, as data, so the App's check-run summary and the log never disagree. `cli`: the body of 'To fix — Option 1, with the CLI (a workspace admin)' exactly as printed (every `missing[].cli` and every note), null when nothing is to fix. `consentUrl`: 'To fix — Option 2, in the browser' — the consent link for THIS run, `<consentBaseUrl>/github/consent/run/<owner>/<repository>/<run_id>` (resolvable by run: the consent id the App mints after the run is unknowable to the job), null when the job had no configured base URL (THORYN_CONSENT_URL — `.thoryn/workflow.yaml` consentUrl / the reusable workflow's consent-url input) or was not a GitHub Actions run.

kind.description: The ADR's grantable set, nothing else: `plan_profile` — a plan profile on the trust for the environment the job ran in (`thoryn workload-identity trusts set-plan-profile`); `owner` — the platform owner relation on an EXISTING object the file declares (access_not_owned on a live id; access_read_only when the identity may only view a resource it is to own; access_owned_elsewhere — then with `cli` null, a dispute an admin decides; SSO-3774: access_not_reachable on a declared workload-identity trust the identity cannot see, named `trust:<name>`); `manager` — on the parent `environment:<id>` of a refused create (never on the workspace); `viewer` — on an existing object declared `readOnly: true` the identity holds no relation on; `creator` (SSO-3792, oauthy ADR 2026-10-17-consent-approved-application-creation-slots §6) — a CREATION SLOT: a workspace admin approves that the subject creates ONE named application (`object` = `application:<clientId>`) on ONE Thoryn plane (`environment`), once, within 30 days (`thoryn access reserve`). Emitted only for an application the file declares with a fixed `clientId`, on the PRODUCTION plane (decision D3), that the identity cannot see and may not create — never `owner` on an application that may not exist (SSO-3787). A consumer that predates the kind drops that ONE item (oauthy SSO-3791) — the rest of the request still reaches the consent.

object.description: The platform object: `application:<clientId>` (for a creator item: the application to be created, its id percent-encoded as the access API spells it), `environment:<id>`, `custom_domain:<workspaceId>`, `trust:<trust-uuid>` (SSO-3774 — a workload-identity trust the identity can see, oauthy ADR 2026-10-16), …, or `trust:<name>` for a trust named by its NAME: a plan_profile when the trust is named, and (SSO-3774) an owner / viewer on a trust the file DECLARES that the identity cannot see — the name is the file's resource name (unique in the file, the trust's name on the API); the consumer re-reads the file at the head sha for the trust's plane and resolves the name to the id as the admin. A `trust:` value that parses as a UUID is an id; anything else is a name. Null when unknown.

subject.description: The identity to grant the right to — the session's `client:<wi_…>`; null for a plan_profile (set on the trust, not granted to a subject) or when the session token was opaque.

environment.description: plan_profile: the GitHub environment the job ran in — the one the profile is for. creator (SSO-3792): the Thoryn plane slug the application is to be created in (`production`). Null for every other kind.

reason.description: Why the right is missing: the engine's row reason (`<code> — …`) or the sign-in's local finding. Names objects and environments, never a secret and never another repository's identity.

cli.description: The exact command a workspace admin runs — the copy-pasteable block the check run relays verbatim and the CLI prints itself. `<trust-id>` where the producer could not resolve the id (`thoryn workload-identity trusts list` shows it) — always so for an item whose object is `trust:<name>`; `<subject>` when the session token was opaque. Null for a dispute the CLI shows but never resolves (an object another repository owns). A creator item's command is `thoryn access reserve <subject> application:<clientId> --environment <plane>`.
